summary: Course and peer sources give distinct routes to spells. The Illusion II practical needs moral accounting, and Lyra’s repeat offer needs to remember the first demonstration.

issues.problem: At Illusion II the practical makes three people falsely remember the player rescuing the cook. This knowingly takes undeserved credit through manipulated memories but has no Hollow consequence, unlike other lying-for-gain choices.
issues.fix: Give this level-specific fabrication its moral consequence, or make it an openly consented classroom illusion test that does not create real false credit.

issues.problem: The right label is always Watch how the hare moves even when the advanced setup and outcome are about a hawk or hippogriff.
issues.fix: Use a species-neutral label such as Study its movement first, or branch the label with the course level.

issues.problem: Declining the lesson leaves this repeat-4 offer eligible, but each opening again claims I’ve never shown anyone after the player has already watched her demonstrate it.
issues.fix: Branch the opening on seen(lyra_teaches_wildfire), with a repeat invitation after the first showing.

issues.problem: The level-I opening says Illusion begins by trying to make Vey like the student, and the left route casts directly on her. The worldbook fact vey.own_face says every student first glamours their own face, because a glamour they cannot hold on themselves will not hold on anyone.
issues.fix: Put the required self-glamour step before trying it on Vey in the introductory practical, or change the introductory exercise to match the established teaching order.
